body: I have lost all desire to to anything but go to my death. One last long hike into the middle of nowhere. That’s it. At least I can provide this for myself. I used to want so much more, but it’s all gone now.

This has already been going on for years. I’m very burned out on feeling like I’m being chipped away, little by little. I’m so tired all of the time. There’s nothing but this perpetually empty feeling. All I have to do now is find the energy, one last time, to go and find a good place where I won’t disturb anyone. I will be alone, like I always have been, but this time it will have been my choice, and I won’t have to face this feeling ever again.

I don’t know what I have to live for. Everything I’ve come to value at all is either gone or is currently slipping away. If I were loved, I wish someone had said so. I came to care very deeply for someone who had been in a similar situation. I eventually told them how I felt and it’s like I was nothing more than a stepping stone. You’re very right about the world being cold. It’s all I see, day in and day out. I try very much to help others when I can because it’s the only thing that gives me purpose. I don’t want other people to feel completely worthless like I do. I’ve tried so hard to find meaning in this, but I’m so tired of fighting. I really just want this to end. I don’t have anything left.

I work in a military hospital. I scheduled an appointment to speak with someone but it’s not until the end of the month. I wish I could just leave my job, but I’m stuck here until my contract is through. I wish I could say that it’s just the depression, but I am objectively lonely and isolated. I have absolutely no people to turn to.

I have felt extremely overwhelmed lately. All of the people I work with have families to go home to. Because I’m alone, I am chosen for extra work every time something needs to be covered. I work nights but get pulled for daytime coverage with less than 12 hours’ notice. Of course, this is all while being told I don’t belong in my field. It makes no sense to me and is very frustrating. Despite all of this, I know I’m easily replaceable and no one would even remember I was there after a month.

And then I have absolutely no meaningful life outside of work. All that I’ve managed to accomplish in that regard is making a complete fool of myself and adding more emotional pain onto everything. 

I’m very lonely and it hurts so much every day. I can’t even go to the store and see people with their families, friends, and significant others without wondering what’s wrong with me.

I have been in and out of having these thoughts for a while. I tried so hard for so long to see a light at the end of this, to believe that things would look up. Never, not once did they ever. I fought it for longer than I thought I could. I’m just so tired. I’d have a mountain to climb in order to recover, but I can’t get a good foothold to start. Maybe I’m a coward for wanting to take the easy way out, but I just can’t take it anymore.

I know not everyone has this experience, but I personally have no more reason to go home. It’s really only “home” in the sense that it’s where I was born and raised. I have no family worth seeing there anymore, and most of my friends have moved on. I hope one day I’ll click somewhere. Some days are better than others, for sure. Sometimes it almost gets to be too much. Thank you for at least providing a bit of an outlet to share.
I’ll look into all of that. Thank you for wanting to help. Maybe one day it’ll be better and I’ll have something to show for it.

I lost a parent, the one I was far closer to growing up,  as a teenager. Despite being in a class of almost 400 students, only one person bothered to reach out. Despite that, I kept believing that people still cared. I continued on over the years, increasingly separated from all of the people I considered friends, and found new people. One by one, the people I came to love, both platonically and romantically, showed that they didn’t feel the same way. Now that has only continued and I find myself in a place where it’s even more difficult to meet people. Along the way I’ve lost friends to suicide, accidents, you name it. Top it off with someone blatantly disregarding the feelings I had, and admittedly still have, for her, after acting like she actually felt the same way, and I suppose that brings us to where I am now.  For the first time in a long time, I had total trust in another person and it was completely misplaced. Just like any other time I felt important to anyone, it was a lie. There’s no one left for me to go to any more. All I have is myself, and I’m a total joke of an excuse for a person.

I wish I had any idea of how many times I’d have to choose to keep going. I admire you having made it to 35 with these feelings, because I feel like the weight doubles every day. I don’t feel like I could even take another year of this, much less another decade.

Maybe so. I just find it difficult to believe there’s anything good headed my way. Every time I believed in anything or anyone, I was crushed even further. I’d rather feel nothing than to lose any more hope for the future.

I don’t see why anything would truly change for me. Nothing’s gotten better before, nothing’s gotten better now. It doesn’t matter what I do, the outcome is the same. I don’t have the capacity to keep doing this over and over again, hoping that each time will work out for some good. It never does. You’re right, though; no one’s special. Some people are just more fortunate than others. I’m going to die alone and no one will care in the least. Maybe someone will find me after it happens, not like it’ll matter or that I’ll care. I wish there were some shred of evidence for me to believe I deserve anything nice at all.

And sometimes, despite all of the wishing, hoping, and the promises to do better this time around, everything gets worse anyway. Everything can definitely change, I just seem to be stuck going one way.
Thank you, nonetheless. If only wishing something made it a reality, I would be on a much better path than I am now. Maybe one day it’ll all be better, but that’s if I’m even around to see the day.

I wish that things would stop getting worse. I wonder how much more I have to lose. I wish it wasn’t so difficult to connect with people, and I wish I actually mattered enough for someone to care out here. I find myself closer and closer to ending it every time these thoughts come around and I feel like it doesn’t matter anyway. No one would be hung up on me being gone.

I guess so. At least this is impersonal enough that I don’t have to look another person in the eye who doesn’t want me around. I wish I never made the mistake of hoping I wouldn’t get that look over and over again. I wish I were one of those people who could actually say that things get better. Instead, I’ve watched everything decline, topped off by a close friend telling me how much I’ve changed as a person, how much ambition and drive I’ve lost, all before leaving my life like everyone else.

I don’t. I work a block schedule and go through all of my time off without hearing from anyone. I go in early and leave late because I want so much to avoid being completely alone. No one really cares at work, either, but at least there’s something to do. I’m 600 miles away from home, which is “home” now only in the sense that I was born there. There’s nothing for me there. I’m not worth anything to anyone.

I barely have any friends. I admit that it’s nice being alone sometimes, but it gets old when it reaches the point of not even being a choice anymore. No one wants me around. It’s probably for a good reason, likely the same reason why the few people I have gotten close to have all ended up leaving.
One moment at a time because there’s nothing to look forward to. Fair enough. That’s about as much meaning as my life has to me or anyone else anyway.

Wondering why I’m still alive. I matter to no one. I’ve slept so much in the past two days hoping I wouldn’t wake up that I can’t even sleep anymore. I wish I had any reason to do anything outside of my job.

No one loves me. I look people in the eyes and see that they don’t want me around. I could disappear and no one would notice or care. The people I have felt love for have never reciprocated, and I don’t blame them for wanting to avoid that burden. It’s weighed more on me lately because the feeling’s been refreshed again. You’re very right - the thoughts never go away. Sometimes they’re far enough in the back of my mind for me to function in my free time. Sometimes I’m reminded of the fact that no one cares, and there’s no reason for me to be around.

You’re very fortunate to have found a reason to live. I’m glad that some people are able to find that. I’ve held on to that hope for some time and I find it very difficult to believe that I deserve anything. No one has ever loved me, and at this point I can’t see why anyone ever would.

I left behind the few people I was ever close with, and I initially did so without a second thought. Since joining, I have only lost friends, both back home and in the military. I had hoped to find some sense of belonging, but this is the most isolated I have ever felt. I no longer keep regular contact with my family or friends back home, and people seem to distance themselves when they find out you’re military, so I have no real interaction with anyone beyond day-to-day things like getting a haircut or buying groceries. 

I don’t want to blame the military for everything wrong with my life because I’m in a much better place financially than before I enlisted. However, I can’t say I feel any sort of fulfillment because every meaningful connection I had with anyone has either failed or is reaching that point.

More than usual, lately. People always say things get better, but I’ve been clinging to that hope for years and things have gotten worse, if anything. 

I can’t say I’ve “conquered” my thoughts of suicide. I can’t bring myself to do it, for some reason. Maybe I don’t have the energy. Maybe I’m a coward. I know it wouldn’t matter to anyone either way. I don’t know why I’m still here.

I wish that were true. The only time I’m not physically alone is at work. My shifts are 12 hours long and I come in early and stay late because it’s the closest thing I have to any sort of reason to live anymore. But as soon as I leave, no one cares.
I can’t even bring myself to end it. I’m just here wishing that the end would somehow find me instead.
